evidence.pashto: Muhammad Jan: “Yesterday you said زه اوبه څښم — I drink water. Today, when speaking to a familiar friend, say ته اوبه څښې — you drink water. The ending changes from ـم to ـې. We can join two complete clauses: ته کوټه پاکوې او زه پر څوکۍ کښېنم — You clean the room, and I sit on the chair. Each clause has its own subject and verb. Use informal ته with peers; when addressing respected elders, a different polite form will be taught tomorrow.”

evidence.pashto: Ms Hameed: “You have learned ته کتاب لولې — you read a book (speaking to one familiar friend). When addressing an elder, a teacher, an unfamiliar adult or several people, use تاسې کتاب لولئ. The polite/plural verb generally ends in ـئ instead of the informal ـې. The same تاسې form can refer to one respected person or a group. Look at the listener and the context. In some speech you will also hear تاسو; we use تاسې for consistency in these lessons.”
